facts.one_liner: Opposite the Tuileries since 1815, the “hotel of kings” with Salvador Dalí’s old suite.
facts.why_go: Founded in 1815 and rebuilt in its current form in 1907, Le Meurice faces the Tuileries Garden between the Louvre and Place de la Concorde. Its Louis XVI interiors, restaurant inspired by the Salon de la Paix at Versailles and suite once used for a month every year by Salvador Dalí make it one of Paris’s most storied palace hotels. It received the official “Palace” distinction in 2011.
facts.best_time: April–June and September–October for the Tuileries at their best.
facts.how_to_get_there: 228 Rue de Rivoli; Tuileries and Concorde Métro stations are steps away. CDG airport is about 45–60 minutes by car.
facts.good_to_know: The Louvre is a five-minute walk through the Tuileries—go early or late to avoid queues.

facts.one_liner: Red geranium-draped balconies on Paris’s haute-couture avenue, with an Eiffel Tower view.
facts.why_go: Opened in 1913 on Avenue Montaigne, the street of the great fashion houses, the Plaza Athénée is instantly recognisable by its red awnings and hundreds of red geraniums tumbling from its balconies. Christian Dior presented his New Look nearby in 1947, and many upper rooms have views of the Eiffel Tower. In winter its courtyard becomes an ice rink.
facts.best_time: Spring for the geraniums at their brightest; late autumn and winter for the courtyard ice rink.
facts.how_to_get_there: 25 Avenue Montaigne, 8th arrondissement; Alma-Marceau and Franklin D. Roosevelt Métro stations are nearby. CDG airport is about 45 minutes by car.
facts.good_to_know: Avenue Montaigne’s boutiques and a Seine river cruise from Pont de l’Alma are all within a short walk.

image.attribution: Photo: The Langham, London, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.proof_notes: Commons file 'File:Langham london.jpg' (6000×4738) confirms The Langham London; visually checked on contact sheet. desc: The Langham, London

facts.one_liner: London’s first grand hotel, where Conan Doyle set scenes of Sherlock Holmes.
facts.why_go: When it opened in 1865, The Langham was London’s largest and most modern hotel, with the first hydraulic lifts in England. Mark Twain, Oscar Wilde and Napoleon III stayed, and Arthur Conan Doyle set parts of two Sherlock Holmes stories here. Its Palm Court has served afternoon tea since 1865, and Artesian is regularly ranked among the world’s best bars.
facts.best_time: Year-round; summer evenings are lovely for walks in nearby Regent’s Park.
facts.how_to_get_there: 1C Portland Place, opposite BBC Broadcasting House; Oxford Circus station is about 5 minutes’ walk. Heathrow is about 45 minutes by car or via the Elizabeth line from Bond Street.
facts.good_to_know: Oxford Street’s shops and the West End theatres are within walking distance.

image.proof_notes: Commons file 'File:Chateau Frontenac at dusk in Quebec City.jpg' (7541×5091) confirms Fairmont Le Château Frontenac; visually checked on contact sheet. desc: The Château Frontenac at dusk. Quebec City, Quebec, Canada.

facts.one_liner: Said to be the world’s most photographed hotel, towering above the St. Lawrence.
facts.why_go: Opened in 1893 by the Canadian Pacific Railway, the Château Frontenac crowns the clifftop of Old Quebec—a UNESCO World Heritage Site—with copper roofs and turrets above the St. Lawrence River. It hosted the Quebec Conferences of 1943 and 1944 between Churchill and Roosevelt and is a National Historic Site of Canada. The Dufferin Terrace boardwalk runs right along its foot.
facts.best_time: June–September for street life and festivals; late January–February for the Quebec Winter Carnival.
facts.how_to_get_there: 1 Rue des Carrières, in Upper Town; Jean Lesage International Airport is about 25 minutes by car, and VIA Rail trains from Montreal take about 3.5 hours.
facts.good_to_know: The Old Quebec funicular links Dufferin Terrace with the Petit-Champlain quarter below.

ad.cta_label: Find a stay in Old Quebec

facts.one_liner: A 19th-century Ottoman sultan’s palace on the Bosphorus with an infinity pool at the water’s edge.
facts.why_go: Built for Sultan Abdülaziz between 1863 and 1867, the marble Çırağan Palace stretches along the European shore of the Bosphorus between Beşiktaş and Ortaköy. Gutted by fire in 1910 and restored in the 1980s, it is now a Kempinski hotel whose Sultan Suite has been ranked among the world’s most expensive. Its infinity pool seems to merge with the strait as ships glide past.
facts.best_time: April–June and September–November, when Istanbul is mild.
facts.how_to_get_there: Çırağan Caddesi, Beşiktaş, about 45–60 minutes by car from Istanbul Airport; Ortaköy’s mosque and waterfront are a short walk.
facts.good_to_know: Take a Bosphorus ferry from nearby Beşiktaş pier for the best view of the palace from the water.

image.proof_notes: Commons file 'File:DSC00120 Brazil Parana Iguassu Falls Hotel Das Cataratas (11223407054).jpg' (4272×2848) confirms Hotel das Cataratas; visually checked on contact sheet. desc: Hotel Das Cataratas is situated in front of Iguassu Falls (side Brazil) and the view of the falls is exceptional

facts.one_liner: The only hotel inside Brazil’s Iguaçu National Park, a short walk from the falls.
facts.why_go: Opened in 1958, this pink Portuguese colonial-style hotel stands within Iguaçu National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, just across the road from the start of the falls trail. Run by Belmond, it gives guests access to the walkways before the park opens and after it closes, when you can have the thundering cascades almost to yourself. Coatis, toucans and butterflies wander through its gardens.
facts.best_time: Year-round; the falls are fullest in the wetter months (roughly December–March), while April–June and August–October are pleasant and less humid.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 15 km from Foz do Iguaçu International Airport (IGU); park rules restrict private cars, so the hotel arranges transfers.
facts.good_to_know: Hotel guests’ park entrance is included; also plan a day on the Argentine side for the Devil’s Throat walkway (bring your passport).

ad.cta_label: Find a stay in Foz do Iguaçu

facts.one_liner: The “Pink Palace of the Pacific” on Waikīkī Beach, open since 1927.
facts.why_go: One of Waikīkī’s first resort hotels, the Royal Hawaiian opened in 1927 with a pink stucco façade in Spanish-Moorish style, set in tropical gardens right on the sand. It has hosted celebrities and dignitaries for nearly a century, and its signature pink touches extend to umbrellas, towels and even banana bread. Its Mai Tai Bar is one of the island’s classic sunset spots.
facts.best_time: Year-round; April–May and September–October are drier and quieter.
facts.how_to_get_there: 2259 Kalākaua Avenue, Waikīkī; Daniel K. Inouye International Airport is about 25 minutes by car.
facts.good_to_know: Surf lessons and outrigger canoe rides launch from the beach in front of the hotel.

facts.one_liner: A white grand hotel beneath Mount Washington, where the IMF and World Bank were born.
facts.why_go: Opened in 1902 at the foot of the Presidential Range in the White Mountains, this Spanish Renaissance Revival hotel hosted the 1944 Bretton Woods Conference, which established the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank. Its long wraparound veranda looks straight at Mount Washington, the highest peak in the northeastern US, and the Mount Washington Cog Railway is close by.
facts.best_time: Late September–mid-October for spectacular autumn colour; winter for skiing at Bretton Woods.
facts.how_to_get_there: On US Route 302 in Bretton Woods, about 2.5–3 hours by car from Boston and about 1.5 hours from Manchester-Boston Regional Airport.
facts.good_to_know: The historic Cog Railway, operating since 1869, climbs to the summit of Mount Washington.

ad.cta_label: Find a stay in Bretton Woods

facts.one_liner: A neo-Manueline fantasy palace hidden in an ancient monastic forest.
facts.why_go: Begun in 1888 as a planned royal residence and completed as a hotel by 1907, the Palace Hotel do Buçaco is a neo-Manueline masterpiece designed by Luigi Manini, the architect of Sintra’s Quinta da Regaleira. Its arcades and spires echo Lisbon’s Jerónimos Monastery, and its rooms are lined with azulejo tile panels by Jorge Colaço. It sits within the walled Buçaco Forest, planted by Carmelite monks from 1628.
facts.best_time: April–October for walks through the forest; the palace is atmospheric in misty autumn.
facts.how_to_get_there: In the Serra do Buçaco near Luso, about 30 minutes by car from Coimbra and 1.5 hours from Porto.
facts.good_to_know: Its cellars hold the hotel’s own Buçaco wines, served only at the palace and sister hotels.

facts.one_liner: A 1927 stone-and-timber grand lodge at the foot of Yosemite’s cliffs.
facts.why_go: Opened in 1927 on the floor of Yosemite Valley, The Ahwahnee is a masterpiece of National Park Service rustic architecture, with granite and timber walls, Native American design motifs and a soaring Great Lounge. Its Dining Room is famous for its sugar-pine trestles and towering windows, and the hotel inspired interiors for The Shining. Half Dome and Yosemite Falls rise just outside.
facts.best_time: Late April–June for waterfalls at full flow; autumn for quieter trails; winter for snowy valley views.
facts.how_to_get_there: In Yosemite Valley, about 4 hours by car from San Francisco; Fresno Yosemite International Airport is about 2.5 hours away.
facts.good_to_know: Check Yosemite’s peak-season entry reservation rules—an in-park lodging booking usually covers them, but the park entrance fee still applies.

ad.cta_label: Find a stay in Yosemite Valley
